Question:
If \(n\) is an even positive integer, the double factorial notation \(n!!\) represents the product of all the even integers from \(2\) to \(n.\) For example:

\[ 8!! = 2 \times 4 \times 6 \times 8 \]

What is the units digit of the following sum?

\[ \begin{aligned} &2!! + 4!! + 6!! + \cdots \\ &\quad {}+ 2018!! + 2020!! + 2022!! \end{aligned} \]
Solution:
Every double factorial from \(10!!\) onward contains a factor of \(10\). Each of those terms therefore ends in \(0\) and contributes nothing to the units digit of the sum.

Only the first four terms matter:

\[
2!!=2,\quad4!!=8,\quad6!!=48,\quad8!!=384.
\]

Their units digits add to \(2+8+8+4=22\), whose units digit is \(2\).

Thus the requested digit is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). When only the last digit is needed, a factor of \(10\) can eliminate many large terms at once.
